15	## Get started

24	|---|---|
25	| `deadreckon start "build the app"` | Kick off a supervised run. Walk away. |
26	| `deadreckon attach latest` | Watch it work live. `Ctrl-D` leaves it running. |
27	| `deadreckon status` | What happened, and the one thing to do next. |
28	| `deadreckon list` | Find recent runs and plans. |
29	| `deadreckon finish latest` | Apply it to your branch, or export it. |
30	
31	For a higher-level read while it runs, `deadreckon attach latest --view narrative` shows cited prose plus an evidence-backed visual map.

50	
51	- **It can't fake the finish.** A separate watchdog (`dr-gate`) holds a secret the agent process can't read and signs the result with it. No valid signature, no "done." The agent literally cannot mark its own work accepted.

```text
1	# deadreckon: Concepts & How It Works
2	
3	The narrative companion to the [README](../README.md). If the README tells you
4	*what to type*, this explains *what deadreckon is doing and why you can trust
5	it*. For step-by-step usage, see [HOWTO](../HOWTO.md).
6	
7	## How it works
8	
9	1. **You write "done" in plain English.** deadreckon compiles it into executable checks: tests that must pass, files that must exist, scripts that must succeed.
10	2. **The agent runs in an isolated worktree**, inside a sandbox. Your real checkout is never touched.
11	3. **Every turn is saved** (state, spend, traces, file provenance, snapshots) so you can attach, kill, resume, undo, or audit any moment.
12	4. **A separate watchdog process (`dr-gate`) decides when the work is done.** It holds a secret the agent process cannot read, and signs the result with that secret. The agent cannot forge the signature, so it cannot mark its own work as accepted.
13	5. **If the checks fail, the loop keeps going.** The agent gets another turn. When the watchdog finally signs off for real, the run is atomically promoted to a reviewable artifact: narrative, decisions, file provenance, full audit trail.
14	
15	The loop is the product. The agent CLI does the coding. deadreckon decides when "done" actually means done.
16	
17	## Why this matters
18	
19	**The agent does the coding. deadreckon decides when it's done.**
20	
21	- **It can't fake the finish.** The watchdog (`dr-gate`) holds a secret the agent process can't read and signs the result with it. No valid signature, no "done." The agent literally cannot forge its own acceptance.
22	- **Walk away for real.** Every turn is saved to disk: state, spend, file lineage, a full snapshot. Close your laptop, lose the network, kill the model, then attach from another terminal and resume from the last completed turn. Nothing replays, nothing is lost.
23	- **You get evidence, not a transcript.** Each accepted run promotes to a reviewable artifact: what changed, why, which prompt touched which file, what it spent. Auditable on disk, not scrolled back in a chat window.
24	- **Bring the agent you already trust.** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, or a raw API key: deadreckon supervises any of them. It owns the boundary, not the intelligence.
25	
26	## Bring your own agent CLI
27	
28	deadreckon owns the run boundary; the CLI does the coding. Route any turn through the agent you already trust:
29	
30	| | Agent CLI (subscription) | Route |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| <img src="assets/providers/claude-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Claude Code** | `cli:claude-code` |
33	| <img src="assets/providers/openai-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Codex** | `cli:codex` |
34	| <img src="assets/providers/gemini-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Gemini CLI** | `cli:gemini` |
35	| <img src="assets/providers/github-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | `cli:copilot` |
36	| <img src="assets/providers/opencode-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **OpenCode** | `cli:opencode` |
37	| <img src="assets/providers/pi-logo.svg" alt="" width="22"> | **Pi** | `cli:pi` |
38	
39	Prefer your own keys? Route directly to **Anthropic** (`anthropic`), **OpenAI** (`openai`), or any **OpenAI-compatible** endpoint (`openai-compatible`, e.g. OpenRouter, llama.cpp, local models). No keys at all? `--smoke` runs the whole harness against a faked provider.
40	
41	Already have history in another tool? `deadreckon import claude-code | codex | cursor` ingests it read-only as a run you can inspect.
42	
43	## The two things that make it different
44	
45	### Write "Done" In English, Verified By A Watchdog The Agent Can't Fool
46	
47	Tell deadreckon what success looks like in plain language. It compiles your sentence into executable checks that an independent watchdog runs:
48	
49	```bash
50	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
51	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
52	deadreckon def-done check
53	deadreckon run "finish the app"
54	```
55	
56	**Why the watchdog matters.** `dr-gate` holds a run-local secret the agent process cannot read, and stamps the result with it. Without a valid stamp, the run can't terminate, and the agent can't produce the stamp itself. If the checks fail, the run doesn't end; the agent gets another turn with a corrective hint.
57	
58	If no acceptance file is configured, the default is "the working directory exists and `cargo test` passes" (when `Cargo.toml` is present). Supported check kinds are `cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, and `shell`. Full reference, packs, and the compiled YAML format: [HOWTO § Done Criteria](../HOWTO.md#done-criteria).
59	
60	### Get An Auditable Artifact, Not A Transcript
61	
62	deadreckon records which model/tool call touched which files, then promotes each accepted run to a review packet:
63	
64	- `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` explains what happened.
65	- `RUN-DECISIONS.md` records the decision ledger: design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions.
66	- `RUN-AS-BUILT.md` captures the subsystem shape after the run.
67	- `provenance.jsonl` links every changed file back to the turn, tool call, and model that produced it.
68	- `manifest.json` records what was built and from what.
69	
70	Agentic CLIs usually leave you with a patch and a transcript. deadreckon turns the session into a local published artifact you can inspect, export, extend, or apply. Doc kinds and the TUI docs view: [HOWTO § Generated Docs](../HOWTO.md#generated-docs).
71	
72	## What else it does
73	
74	Each of these is a first-class capability; usage lives in [HOWTO](../HOWTO.md):
75	
76	- **Your checkout is never touched.** Runs default to an isolated `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch; your real checkout changes only when you `deadreckon apply`. Copy, fresh, and explicit in-place modes are available too.
77	- **Crash-proof.** Every turn writes durable state. If the terminal dies, attach from another; if the run crashes, resume from the last completed turn.
78	- **Budgets and time limits.** `--max-spend 15` and `--max-wall-seconds 1800` cap a run, then walk away. High spend requires explicit confirmation.
79	- **Undo a single bad turn.** Snapshot-based rollback to any turn (`deadreckon undo --run <id> --turn 3`), recorded in the run trace, not just a `git reset`.
80	- **Resume, kill, extend, or export any run.** Runs are lifecycle objects, not one terminal session.
81	- **Autonomous chains for multi-step work.** Break a big goal into ordered steps, each with its own signed gate; the chain stops on the first gate failure.
82	
83	## The mental model
84	
85	```text
86	your repo
87	  |
88	  | deadreckon def-done "what 'finished' looks like, in English"
89	  | deadreckon run  "what to build"
90	  v
91	isolated worktree or copy   ◄── your real checkout untouched
92	  |
93	  | provider route: cli:codex, cli:claude-code, cli:gemini, anthropic, openai, ...
94	  v
95	sandboxed turn loop         ◄── agent works here
96	  |
97	  | every turn: trace, spend, provenance, snapshot, docs
98	  | check fails? agent gets another turn
99	  v
100	dr-gate watchdog            ◄── separate process, holds hidden nonce
101	  |                              agent CANNOT produce a valid marker
102	  | checks pass + signature valid?
103	  v
104	promoted artifact           ◄── narrative, decisions, file lineage
105	  |
106	  | inspect, doc, apply, discard, extend, export, cleanup
107	  v
108	your branch or library
109	```
110	
111	For multi-step work, `deadreckon chain` wraps this whole loop and runs N of them in order, stopping on the first gate failure. The agent owns the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.
112	
113	## Compared with agentic coding CLIs
114	
115	deadreckon doesn't replace Claude Code, Codex, or the rest; it supervises them. Use it when the task is too long, risky, or expensive to "run the agent in my checkout and hope I can reconstruct what happened."
116	
117	| Operational concern | Agentic CLI alone | deadreckon supervising the CLI |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| Workspace safety | Often runs where you start it | Isolated worktree by default; your checkout untouched |
120	| Long-running attach | Tied to the current terminal | Durable state; attach from another terminal later |
121	| Spend control | Varies by provider | Tracks totals; enforces spend and wall-clock caps |
122	| Undo | git-level or manual | Snapshots every turn; restores a specific turn |
123	| Done criteria | The agent may declare itself done | Requires a signed `dr-gate` marker before promotion |
124	| Output | A patch and a transcript | A promoted, auditable artifact with file provenance |
125	
126	Use the agentic CLI for intelligence. Use deadreckon for isolation, supervision, evidence, recovery, and promotion.
127	
128	## Why "deadreckon"?
129	
130	Dead reckoning is navigation without perfect visibility: track every move so you know where you are now. Unattended agents are the same problem: long task, partial context, the terminal may be gone when you look back. The name is the contract: don't trust the final answer, navigate by evidence.
131
```

I now have a comprehensive understanding of the codebase. Let me give you the picture.

## DeadReckon — what it is

**A supervision harness for coding agents.** It wraps the agent CLI you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, or any raw Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible API) so you can run it *unattended* and *trust the result*. The tagline captures it: **"Run your coding agent unattended, and trust the result."**

The core insight: an agent declaring its own work "done" is unverifiable. DeadReckon takes the *decision of when work is finished* away from the agent and gives it to a separate watchdog process.

It's a **Rust workspace** (~119k LOC) of 5 crates:

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `deadreckon` | The CLI + TUI (`attach`, narrative view, cards). Also ships the `dr-gate` binary. |
| `deadreckon-core` | State, gate/signing, artifacts, provenance, git, chains, campaigns, learning |
| `deadreckon-runtime` | The **turn loop** — drives the agent, runs the gate each turn, handles compaction/seams |
| `deadreckon-providers` | Provider routing: CLI agents, HTTP APIs, scripted "smoke" fake |
| `deadreckon-sandbox` | Sandboxing/isolation policy and process control |

## How it works (the lifecycle)

1. **You write "done" in plain English** → compiled into executable checks (`acceptance.yaml`). Supported kinds: `cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, `shell`.
2. **The agent runs in an isolated `git worktree`** on a `dr/...` branch inside a sandbox — your real checkout is never touched.
3. **Every turn writes durable state** (trace, spend, file provenance, snapshots) — so you can attach from another terminal, kill, resume from the last completed turn, or undo a single turn.
4. **A separate watchdog (`dr-gate`) decides "done."** This is the key differentiator (see below).
5. **On real acceptance, the run is promoted to an auditable artifact**: `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, `RUN-DECISIONS.md`, `RUN-AS-BUILT.md`, `provenance.jsonl`, `manifest.json`. Then you `apply` it to your branch or export it.

## The watchdog trick (why "it can't fake the finish")

This is the architecturally interesting part. Looking at the code:

- `dr-gate` (`crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs`) is a **separate process** spawned by the turn loop each turn. It evaluates the acceptance checks, runs a tamper check, and only on success calls `write_acceptance_marker_with_results`.
- The marker is **signed** (`gate.rs:762` `marker_signature`) by hashing the marker fields together with a **run-local nonce** read from `<run-root>/gate/nonce`.
- The turn loop validates the marker (`validate_acceptance_marker`, `gate.rs:148`): it must be `status: pass`, `produced_by: dr-gate`, and have a signature that recomputes correctly. A forged self-attestation is refused.
- The signature also binds the **tamper verdict file** and the **campaign rollup** — so neither can be edited after signing to launder a failed run into a clean pass.

So the agent process literally cannot produce a valid "done" marker — no valid signature, no termination. If checks fail, the loop pushes a corrective hint into history (`turn_loop.rs:1681`) and the agent gets another turn.

## The CLI surface

Five headline commands (`start`, `attach`, `status`, `list`, `finish`), but it's much deeper: `def-done`, `run`, `chain` (multi-step, each step its own signed gate), `plan`/`fork`/`merge` (multi-agent orchestration), `campaign`, `undo`/`rewind` (flight recorder), `learn`/`improve` (self-improvement loop), `import` (ingest history from Claude Code/Codex/Cursor read-only), plus full lifecycle ops (`kill`, `resume`, `extend`, `apply`, `abandon`, `cleanup`, `export`).
